heading: Ancestry
intro: My sister and I are often asked where we are from. This question sometimes opens into a longer conversation, because the two halves of our heritage are quite different from one another, and together they produce a genetic profile that tends to confuse people. The detail below is my personal attempt to give that conversation a proper home, using my 23AndMe results. The short answer: {bold}. I am originally from Quebec but, lived and educated mostly in Ontario. My father and grandfather are from Alberta. My paternal great-grandparents came from Germany and initially settled in the United States before migrating further north to become founding settlers of Bruderheim, Alberta. My mother is a naturalized Canadian citizen, originally from India. Most of my education took place in Ontario. I only speak, write, and think in English. I use Duolingo to dabble in French and German, more French than German, but I am not bilingual or multilingual, an Anglophone. However, I translate the Alpha-El app into French, with attention to details, as best I can, with the assistance of translation tools. This is to be in compliance and respectful of Canadian bilingual requirements. I am proud of my diverse heritage, and inspired by the accomplishments of my ancestors, on both sides of my family.
starTrekQuote: "We will add your biological and technological distinctiveness to our own. Your culture will adapt to service us. Resistance is futile."

germanDesc1: My father's family is of German descent, with roots concentrated in northwestern Germany. 23andMe confirms two strong Genetic Group matches: {g1} and {g2} (both rated {rating}), with country matches to {country}.
germanDesc2: The Maschmeyer name itself is traceable to the Lower Saxony / Westphalia region. Maschmeyer, translated as "Mayer of the marshland"; see Maschmeyer's Mühle historic site located in the Teutoburg Forest. A 23andMe diaspora signal, {diaspora} (Very Close), reflects the large 19th-century wave of German emigrants who settled the American Midwest before some branches continued north into Canada.
germanDesc2Diaspora: Lower Missouri River Basin Early German Americans
parsiDesc1: My mother's family are {parsi}, members of the Zoroastrian community that emigrated from Persia (present-day Iran) to the Indian subcontinent, primarily settling around Bombay (now Mumbai) roughly 1,000 to 1,300 years ago. The Parsi community is one of the smallest and most genetically distinct ethno-religious groups in the world.
parsiDesc2: 23andMe identifies {group} as a {rating} Genetic Group match and places a Country Match on {country}. The large {comp} component (~37.5%) is the genetic signature of the original Persian homeland. Parsis carry this ancestry intact because the community historically married within itself, preserving a genetic profile closer to ancient Iran than to the surrounding South Asian population.
